description: Schema for credential daemon provider test cases

documentation.description: What the case checks, and which spec rule it covers

appliesTo.description: Only these SDKs run the case (SDK identifiers, for example 'ruby'). Absent: every SDK

sdkSpecific.description: The expected outcome depends on the SDK's existing behavior (see the SEP's notes on implementation). The outcome given is botocore's

requiresCredentialRefresh.description: The case needs the Credential Refresh SEP. Until that SEP is released in the SDK, runners run the case and report it as an expected failure, not skipped or removed; once it is released, the case MUST pass

platform.description: Operating system the SDK believes it runs on. The socket lookup is the same on Linux and macOS, so a runner MAY run any case on either

environment.description: Environment variables set for the test. AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET values 'env' (an absolute temporary path) and 'relative' (a relative path; the 'env' socket is then created at that path under the current directory) are logical; the empty string is literal. HOME value 'relative' is a relative path; the 'link' socket is then created at .aws/credential-daemon.sock under the current directory

unsetEnvironment.description: Environment variables unset for the test. With HOME unset, the 'link' socket is created at .aws/credential-daemon.sock under the current directory

credentialsContents.description: Shared credentials file contents (INI), if any

profile.description: Profile the SDK resolves, through AWS_PROFILE unless explicitProfile is true

explicitProfile.description: The profile is set in code (for example Session(profile=...)) instead of AWS_PROFILE

nextProvider.description: A stub for the next provider in the default chain (container or IMDS). If the outcome says terminal, it MUST NOT be called, except in SDKs that move on after provider errors (see the SEP's Errors section), which assert instead that the same profile's other credential settings aren't used

invalidatedAccessKeyId.description: Optional. Access key ID of cached daemon credentials that a service rejected. The case is the refresh that follows that invalidation, with no refresh backoff active

sockets.description: Logical sockets that exist. 'link' ($HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock, a symbolic link to a socket in a temporary folder), 'link-dangling' (that link, pointing at missing-daemon.sock in a temporary folder, which doesn't exist), 'home-socket' (a socket, not a link, at $HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock), 'env' (AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET). 'stale' means the path exists but nothing listens; 'file' means a regular file is at the path

exchanges.description: The one request the SDK MUST send on the connection, and the raw lines the fake sends back

expectedRequest.description: method and params the SDK MUST send. params MUST match exactly, with no other keys. id is not compared; the fake echoes it where a reply line has id '$id'

replyLines.description: Each item is one line the fake writes, without the newline. A string is written as is; an object is serialized. '$id' in an object's id is replaced with the request's id. An object with "$padTo": n has that key removed and a string field 'padding' of 'x' characters added to its result, so the serialized line is n bytes, not counting the newline

close.description: The fake closes the connection after writing the reply lines. With no reply lines, it closes without sending any

result.description: notResolved: the daemon provider returns no credentials and the chain moves on

dialed.description: Which logical socket the SDK MUST dial

source.description: Where the resolved credentials came from

errorKind.description: ssoConfig is the SSO provider's existing error and has no errorCode. refreshFailed is the SDK's usual recoverable refresh failure and has no errorCode

errorCode.description: The code the error MUST carry: the Code column of the SEP's Errors table. An unknown data.code is REQUEST_REJECTED

messageContains.description: Substrings the error message SHOULD contain. One taken from the daemon's message in a daemon error reply MUST be there (see the SEP's Errors section)

messageNotContains.description: Substrings the error message MUST NOT contain

featureIds.description: User-agent feature ID values the request signed with these credentials MUST carry, in order. Only for SDKs that support User Agent 2.1

terminal.description: The next provider MUST NOT be called, except in SDKs that move on after provider errors (see the SEP's Errors section), which assert instead that the same profile's other credential settings aren't used
